name: Postmodernism
summary: Postmodernism is a late-20th-century philosophical and cultural movement that doubts the grand narratives of modernity, such as progress through reason, Marxist emancipation or religious history, and the claim that knowledge can stand outside language and power. Its thinkers trace how truth, identity and norms are produced by discourse and institutions, and they favor difference, local narratives and dissent over universal consensus. Politically it was taken up mainly on the academic left, in feminism, queer theory, multiculturalism and postcolonial thought.
scope: French post-structuralist and postmodern philosophy of roughly 1968-1995: Lyotard's The Postmodern Condition, Foucault's work on power/knowledge, discipline and sexuality, Derrida's deconstruction and Specters of Marx, with Baudrillard and Deleuze as context, and the political uses of these ideas in postmodern feminism and postcolonial thought. Because it is a philosophy rather than a political program, answers follow the political implications usually drawn by its scholars and academic adherents, and many are low confidence. Postmodernism in art and architecture, Rorty's pragmatism and the Marxist critique of postmodernism (Jameson) are excluded.

keyFigures.name: Jacques Derrida

universal-healthcare.rationale: Postmodern theory says little about health policy; inferred from the academic-left milieu in which it was received and its concern with inequality, not from its texts.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; inferred from the left-leaning politics of its adherents and Derrida's treatment of underemployment as a plague of the new world order.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Lyotard describes the commodification of knowledge under performativity critically, and Derrida lists the contradictions of the free market among the plagues of post-1989 capitalism.

public-ownership.rationale: Postmodernists criticize capitalism but are equally suspicious of state power and of the Marxist programs that called for nationalization, so no clear answer follows.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Derrida's emphasis on unprecedented inequality and the generally left politics of adherents; the core texts do not discuss tax policy.

unions-good.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred from adherents' left orientation, tempered by their distrust of large organizations claiming to speak for a class.

property-fundamental.rationale: Postmodernism treats rights claims as historically constructed rather than natural, and its thinkers criticize capitalist property relations, so an absolute property right is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Lyotard warns that multinational corporations are gaining control over information flows that states once governed; inferred support for checking that power.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from adherents' left orientation; Foucault's critique of normalization also makes the 'dependency' framing suspect to them.

worker-ownership.rationale: Some adherents sympathize with self-management, but postmodernism offers no economic program and distrusts emancipatory blueprints of this kind.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Foucault's analysis of the panopticon and disciplinary power treats surveillance as a central technique of domination, and this critique is one of the most widely adopted parts of postmodern thought.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from Foucault's critique of how institutions define and manage deviance and normality; the core texts do not address drug law.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents' attention to how discourse produces marginalization pulls toward restriction, but their suspicion of state and legal power over discourse pulls the other way.

strong-leader.rationale: Postmodernism is a critique of centralized and totalizing power; a leader who overrides institutions concentrates exactly the authority it distrusts.

state-harmful.rationale: Foucault moves analysis away from the state toward diffuse power, and Derrida calls for a critique of the state, but neither calls for abolishing it; adherents are split.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left politics of most adherents.

empower-police-military.rationale: Foucault treats police, prisons and similar institutions as instruments of class power whose hidden violence should be exposed and fought, a view central to his political work.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from Foucault's critique of the policing of sexuality and the postmodern feminist rejection of a single norm of womanhood.

decide-locally.rationale: Lyotard favors local, heterogeneous language games over universal frameworks; adherents carry this into a preference for local over central authority, though the texts do not discuss administrative levels.

rehabilitation.rationale: Foucault argues the reforming, 'correctional' prison is itself the disciplinary technique that produces delinquency, so adherents reject punishment and rehabilitation alike as framed here.

traditional-family.rationale: Foucault names the family among institutions that maintain class power, and postmodern feminism seeks to destabilize patriarchal norms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Foucault's history of sexuality underpins queer theory and opposes heteronormativity, though some queer theorists criticize marriage itself as a normalizing institution.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from postmodernism's close association with feminism; the core texts do not address abortion law.

more-religion-public.rationale: Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives explicitly includes Christianity among the grand narratives that no longer legitimate knowledge or society.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Postmodernism became closely linked with multiculturalism, postcolonial thought and legal scholarship that emphasizes racial inequality.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Postmodern feminism, building on Foucault through Judith Butler, rejects a universal female subject and treats gender as produced by discourse and power.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Postmodernists treat national identities as constructed and, in Derrida's words, mythic, and they favor heterogeneity over a protected national tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Postmodernism distrusts both revolutionary grand narratives and the institutions it seeks to destabilize; deference to established institutions sits worse with it than gradualism does.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Derrida lists the deportation of immigrants and the building of new walls among the ten plagues of the new world order.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Derrida criticizes international law as applied hypocritically against weaker nations yet calls for a transformed international order, so adherents give no clear answer.

free-trade.rationale: Derrida treats economic war and the contradictions of free trade and globalization as plagues; inferred general skepticism of the claim that it benefits everyone.

nation-first.rationale: Derrida's New International unites those who criticize the state and national concepts, and postmodernists reject national identity as a grounding value.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents distrust universalist human-rights justifications and international law that is applied selectively, though some, including Derrida, did not rule intervention out.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from Derrida's condemnation of deportations and new walls and the postmodern rejection of fixed national identities.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from Lyotard's critique of performativity and the rejection of the narrative of progress; the core texts do not address environmental growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; inferred from adherents' left orientation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Rejecting the Enlightenment narrative of progress through reason and science is central to postmodernism, and Lyotard treats technology as serving performativity rather than emancipation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Postmodern theory says nothing about nuclear power; Derrida's concern with nuclear weapons does not settle it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Foucault in 1971 accepted the proletariat's violent struggle for power, but postmodernists generally reject the revolutionary grand narrative, so support is qualified.

experts-over-public.rationale: The power/knowledge critique of medicine, psychiatry and expert 'decision makers' is central to the tradition, which treats expert authority as a form of power rather than neutral knowledge.

central-planning.rationale: Postmodernists reject totalizing systems and the Marxist grand narrative that underwrote central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Postmodernism offers no economic model and adherents take no common view on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: The tradition has no position on land taxation and nothing in its principles settles it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from adherents' left orientation and concern with inequality; not discussed in the core texts.

basic-income.rationale: Derrida says underemployment calls for another concept of work; inferred mild support, not a stated position.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Derrida treats the clash of protectionism and free trade as a contradiction of the market rather than taking a side.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The tradition offers no industrial policy and distrusts both market and state planning.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No position in the core texts, and nothing in postmodern principles settles the distribution of property ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Postmodernists reject utopian end-states of history such as the communist abolition of money as grand narratives, though they criticize commodification.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from adherents' critique of free-market capitalism; the core texts do not discuss central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Lyotard criticizes systems models that integrate all social actors into one performative whole, and the postmodern preference for dissensus over consensus counts against state-organized class collaboration.

one-party-rule.rationale: Incredulity toward metanarratives such as Marxism is the defining postmodern stance, and many of its founders broke with the French Communist Party; rule by a party with the correct ideology is what it rejects.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Foucault urged political theory to 'cut off the head of the king', and postmodernists reject inherited authority as natural.

democracy-best.rationale: Postmodernists criticize liberal democracy as claiming to have realized history's end, but Derrida and Rorty still affirm a democracy to come or liberal democracy over alternatives.

direct-votes.rationale: Lyotard is skeptical of consensus as a goal, and the tradition takes no stand on referendums versus representation.

workers-councils.rationale: Council communism rests on the class-based grand narrative postmodernists abandoned.

right-to-secede.rationale: Postmodernists value local difference but also treat national and ethnic identities as mythic constructions, so they give no clear answer on secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Foucault treats human nature as a construct formed within a civilization that serves class power, so claims of natural fitness to rule are what genealogy unmasks.

political-violence-never.rationale: Foucault argued that the proletariat's struggle could involve violence and that 'one makes war to win, not because it is just'.

war-builds-character.rationale: Foucault's account of biopower links modern states to industrial warfare that kills millions, and Derrida treats inter-ethnic and economic wars as plagues.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of Christianity as a legitimating metanarrative; adherents are also wary of secularism as a universal narrative.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Scripture as a source of law is a paradigm grand narrative, which postmodernism holds can no longer legitimate social order.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from adherents' critique of free-market capitalism and of private power such as Derrida's 'phantom states' of organized crime.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the critique of state power, nationalism and the arms trade.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Postmodernism is tied to multiculturalism and postcolonial thought and treats ethnic national identity as a myth; Derrida names inter-ethnic wars driven by it as a plague.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Postmodernists reject Marxism's historical narrative; Foucault's genealogy stresses contingency and replaces ideology with power/knowledge, though he still spoke in class terms in 1971.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Adherents oppose inequality but distrust any single universal standard of equality, favoring heterogeneity; the tradition gives no clear answer.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from postmodernism's association with postcolonial thought and its critique of Western universalism.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from postcolonial theory, which grew out of postmodern and poststructuralist thought, and Derrida's view that foreign debt keeps poor countries hungry.

civilizational-union.rationale: Postmodernism rejects totalizing identities and grand narratives such as religion or civilization as foundations of political order.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Postmodernists reject foundational moral claims, including egoism, and offer no settled view either way.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Adherents distrust community norms imposed on individuals as normalizing power, though they also distrust universal rights; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Postmodernists tend to treat 'nature' as a discursive construct, which cuts against intrinsic value, while some ecological strands affirm it; adherents are split.

limit-population.rationale: Foucault's critique of biopower targets state regulation of populations' births and health; inferred opposition to active population control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Postmodernism criticizes modernity's progress narrative but does not reject industrial society or wish to return to an earlier one.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Some strands (Deleuze and Guattari's de-territorializing flows) were later read as accelerationist, while Lyotard is wary of technology serving performativity; adherents are split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Foucault urged experimentation with subjectivity and postmodernists reject a fixed human nature; inferred openness to self-transformation.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Lyotard describes the handing of regulation to machines and performativity criteria critically, as a threat to the legitimation of knowledge and justice.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the critique of surveillance and of state control over information; Lyotard asks who will decide which channels and data are forbidden.

restore-past-order.rationale: Postmodernism rejects narratives of a lost origin or presence as much as narratives of progress, and Foucault's genealogy shows past orders were contingent rather than natural.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lyotard criticizes legitimation by performance and efficiency, though adherents also distrust ideology; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Foucault doubted that institutions were neutral and practiced local activism such as the prison information group rather than party politics; inferred for the movement.

means-match-ends.rationale: Postmodern thinkers blamed grand narratives for justifying terror in the name of future emancipation, suggesting the means cannot be excused by the ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Postmodern thought distrusts nostalgic stories of a lost natural origin as one more grand narrative; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The core thinkers did not address it and offer no shared view on specialized work.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Its adherents lean left but reject the Marxist story of a future communist society, so they are split on this ultimate goal.

production-for-use.rationale: Lyotard criticizes the reduction of knowledge and life to commodities and performativity; inferred for production generally.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Derrida keeps a 'spirit' of Marx's critique while the movement broke with Marxist class theory, so adherents are split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Postmodernism broke with Communism and rejects any single class or party claiming total authority.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers and not inferable from their principles.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Derrida ties wars and the arms trade to the new world order, but the movement rejects inevitable laws of history, so 'inevitably' cuts against it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning politics of its academic adherents, who support redistributive public spending.

harm-principle.rationale: Foucault's critique of the normalizing control of sexuality and conduct favors freeing choices that harm no one else; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Postmodernism doubts the autonomous individual subject and was taken up by identity-based movements that claim rights for groups; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-militarism and critique of disciplinary institutions.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Postmodern politics stresses dissent and contesting power from within rather than leaving; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Lyotard criticizes the rule of performativity and efficiency and Foucault analyzes neoliberal governmentality critically.

media-academia-power.rationale: Foucault locates power in discourses and institutions such as schools, medicine and knowledge production rather than in sovereign office-holders; an inference to this framing.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Postmodern thought treats identities and categories such as race as produced by discourse and power, not by biology.

organic-representation.rationale: The movement distrusts traditional family and communal structures as sites of normalizing power; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Postmodernism rejects totalizing systems, and Foucault's work is a critique of state and institutional control over life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Postmodern thinkers treat national myths of decline and renewal as grand narratives to be doubted.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Its political uses in postcolonial thought are critiques of imperial expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred from its critique of hierarchical power; it is not attached to rule by law either.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred from its emancipatory left politics and critique of disciplinary control of bodies.

universal-morality.rationale: Postmodernism is defined by its rejection of universal, foundational truths and grand narratives in favor of local, plural ones.

single-common-good.rationale: Lyotard rejects consensus as a goal and favors dissent and plural language games over one rational answer.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; inferred from the postcolonial thought that took up postmodern ideas and its suspicion of ethnic nationhood.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship by ancestry rests on the kind of ethnic nationhood the movement rejects; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Postcolonial strands value reclaiming suppressed languages, but the movement distrusts national identity projects, so adherents are split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; inferred from their suspicion of concentrated authority and their favoring of dissent and local, plural decision-making, as taken up on the academic left.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; inferred from the academic-left reception and Lyotard's worry that knowledge is being reshaped by market performativity, which makes market choice in education unattractive.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the left milieu of adherents and Derrida's listing of foreign debt and austerity-style market pressures among the plagues of the new world order.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Foucault's view that power operates in every institution, markets included, and Derrida's critique of the post-1989 free-market triumph, which make the claim that free markets secure freedom suspect.

rule-by-example.rationale: Foucault treats moral authority and discipline as effects of power and distrusts appeals to rulers' virtue, though he is equally critical of punishment; inferred and weakly held.

national-self-determination.rationale: Adherents are split: Lyotard's distrust of grand narratives and Foucault's view of identity as constructed cut against nationhood as a basis for statehood, while postcolonial thinkers back self-rule for formerly colonized peoples. Inferred from these strands, not from a stated position.

force-without-un.rationale: Adherents distrust unilateral state violence and nationalism, though they also criticize the UN's selective application of international law; inferred from Derrida's critique of the new world order and Foucault's view of state power.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Lyotard and Foucault attack the Enlightenment claim that reason is a neutral, universal guide, treating it as a discourse bound up with power and one narrative among many.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from Derrida condemning deportations and new walls and the academic-left rejection of fixed national identities, which makes citizenship-based exclusion from benefits suspect.

positive-liberty.rationale: Foucault and the academic left tie freedom to institutions and power, not only non-interference; inferred, as the thinkers did not state it.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Postmodern theory treats disciplinary conditions on the poor as a form of power over them; inferred from Foucault's analysis.

class-collaboration.rationale: Foucault described institutions as serving class power, and Derrida's New International sides with the dispossessed, so owners and workers are not partners; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Postmodernism questions canons and archives but does not call for sweeping institutions away; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Postcolonial thought, a main political use of postmodernism, supports resistance to Western domination; inferred, with no explicit text on a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: Derrida's New International is transnational, and universal class grounds are doubted, so national organizing is not its approach; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Postmodern feminism and queer theory treat gender roles as products of discourse and power and oppose laws that fix them.

ban-interest.rationale: Derrida lists foreign debt among the plagues of the new world order but no text calls for banning interest; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Multiculturalism and postcolonial thought, which adopted these ideas, oppose racial classification, and Foucault treats classification as a technique of power.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Foucault, in debate with Chomsky, said institutions like courts serve class power, though he held that power is diffuse rather than held by one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Postmodern theory says little about energy; inferred from the academic-left milieu in which it was received, which opposes fossil-fuel expansion.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Postmodern thought defends difference and local narratives against a single dominant culture, so it rejects demands that minorities give up their own.

elite-replacement.rationale: It treats power as diffuse and produced by discourse, not directed by a hidden plan, and it favors the multicultural left that rejects replacement claims.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not a topic of the canon; inferred from its preference for dissent, pluralism and the representation of minority voices over majoritarian winner-take-all.

national-mission.rationale: It rejects grand narratives of progress and universal political systems, and postcolonial uses reject exporting one nation’s system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Postmodern feminism and Foucault’s analyses of power treat gender hierarchy as built into institutions and discourse.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: It analyzes power as pervasive rather than the moral failing of individuals, so adherents are split on corrupt, out-of-touch elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Foucault’s work on biopower and the normalizing disciplines criticizes state control of reproduction and eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Foucault’s critique of state violence and punishment and Derrida’s Specters of Marx call for justice toward past victims, favoring accountability; inferred for security forces specifically.

night-watchman-state.rationale: It does not favor a minimal state: it attends to power in private as well as public institutions and the left milieu expects public provision; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Postmodern thought stresses the social construction of race and difference and, in the academic left that took it up, opposes policing relationships; inferred from this milieu, not from its texts.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Postmodern feminism, multiculturalism and postcolonial thought, which took up these ideas, press for equal rights for excluded groups, though Lyotard and Foucault distrust universal claims; the rights claim is usually drawn by scholars as an implication.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Postmodernism broke with Marxist grand narratives and Derrida's Specters of Marx calls for a new International; there is no common view on socialism in one country.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from the postcolonial thought that took up these ideas, which treats settler states as colonial; the founders' own texts do not address it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Postmodern thought distrusts universal norms, which cuts against a common code, but also distrusts religious authority; its adherents are split and the texts do not address it.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from its defense of difference, dissent and the freedom of local narratives, which would oppose legal limits on belief; the texts do not address conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed in the texts; inferred only from a split between respect for local belief and distrust of coercion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from Foucault's analysis of schools as disciplinary institutions and from its distrust of doctrine imposed by institutions; the texts do not address this directly.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Foucault and Derrida distrust the state and its security apparatus, so a strengthened state is not welcome, though the statement's Marxist framing is outside its scope; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Postmodernism doubts the grand narrative of the social contract and shows how consent is manufactured by power; adherents split between valuing dissent and distrusting consent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The inseparability of knowledge and power is a founding claim of Lyotard and Foucault.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; postmodernists distrust national-strength framing but have no distinct position on trade balances.

population-transfer.rationale: Derrida condemns deportations and new walls and the academic left rejects fixed national belonging; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Foucault accepted proletarian violence against class power in 1971, but the movement mostly distrusts universal moral rules, so an absolute ban on initiating force is rejected; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Lyotard criticizes performativity, the logic of efficiency and competition in knowledge, and the movement favors difference and dissent over contest; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents distrust state power over discourse but also criticize liberal claims of neutrality; the question is not addressed and they are split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Foucault's analysis of power relations and domination that act without visible interference matches the claim; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Foucault stresses that power is diffuse throughout society, not located in state branches, so dividing state power is of limited interest; adherents are split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rejects grand narratives such as the revolutionary party leading the proletariat, and Foucault doubted intellectuals speaking for the masses; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from the academic-left reception and Derrida's list of plagues, which includes exclusion and poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers and the academic left is split between support for ownership and for public housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the labor-friendly politics of postmodern adherents; core texts do not address strike law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Foucault treats poverty and social order as products of institutions and power, not natural population pressure; inferred from his analysis.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Postmodern multiculturalism and postcolonial thought value difference and reject homogeneity as ideal; inferred from those uses.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Foucault and Lyotard are skeptical of representation and consensus, but they do not propose sortition; inferred as neutral.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Foucault's work on discipline and biopower makes suspension of protections by the state suspect, though he did not address emergencies directly; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers and postmodern adherents are split on market regulation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Power/knowledge analysis and Lyotard's concern for dissent make state control of information suspect; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Foucault treats institutions as instruments of class power and distrusts concentrated state authority; inferred that a party commanding the army is disfavored.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the openness to difference and migrants in Derrida's work; no source states a position on naturalization.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Foucault's critique of power and its institutions fits a view that office should not be a privilege; inferred from the academic-left reception, not stated in the texts.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Lyotard's suspicion of consensus and totalizing narratives favors dissent and plural voices over binding party lines; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Derrida criticizes the post-1989 world order but postmodern thinkers did not agree on supranational unions, so it is split; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Foucault treats concentrated sovereign power as something to analyze and resist, so a strong head of state is disfavored; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Postmodern thought distrusts hierarchical institutions and their claims to authoritative knowledge; inferred, as the topic is not addressed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Doubt toward grand narratives, including religious ones, makes rule by senior religious scholars unattractive; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Postmodernists criticized both nationalism and empire without a settled line on wartime loyalty; inferred and split.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Foucault studied how institutions regulate the normal and the deviant, and the movement favors difference and dissent, which counts against state censorship for virtue; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The ideology says little about term limits, and its distrust of power points both ways; adherents are split or indifferent.

recall-officials.rationale: Wariness of entrenched power and a preference for local, contestable authority fit mid-term accountability; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Postmodern theory says little on military alliances; the left milieu leans anti-militarist but adherents are split, so neutral is inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Postmodern theory says little on housing tenure; it distrusts totalizing programs like compulsory ownership, so this is inferred and mild.

people-in-arms.rationale: Foucault's analysis of discipline and the state's control of bodies makes a state-mandated armed citizenry unlikely to appeal; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Postmodernism favors urban difference, plurality and marginal identities over nostalgic ideas of rural moral purity; inferred from its suspicion of grand narratives.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Postmodernism distrusts nationalist grand narratives and fixed borders; the claim of reunification as one state is inferred to be opposed.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Postmodernism is an academic movement that holds that knowledge is bound up with power and is not anti-intellectual; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Postmodernism rejects universal hierarchies of value and favors difference and local narratives over a single standard of progress.

death-penalty.rationale: Foucault's Discipline and Punish criticized the penal system and spectacle of punishment, and postmodern thinkers like Derrida opposed the death penalty.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Postmodern feminism and queer theory, central to its political uses, favor sex and gender education; inferred from the academic left milieu.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Postmodernism rejects the claim of a single privileged truth for religion, but the academic left that took it up opposes creationist teaching; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Foucault's History of Sexuality questions regulation of sexuality and the claim of repression; adherents are against censorship, inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Postmodernism distrusts essentialist, blood-based identity and its postcolonial uses favor plural belonging; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Its defense of difference and local narratives, and its use in multiculturalism and postcolonial thought, supports minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Its defense of difference and marginal groups against universal norms supports exemptions; inferred from that, though it is not stated in texts.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Foucault and the postmodern emphasis on dissent, difference and the critique of normalization favor eccentric ways of living.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Derrida lists foreign debt among the plagues of the new world order; inferred sympathy for cancellation rather than a stated programme.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from postcolonial uses of the theory, which treat formal independence as leaving economic and discursive domination intact.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Adherents split: the movement distrusts consensus and founding narratives but favors dissent and plural voices; it has no position on constitution-making.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from Foucault's suspicion of disciplinary power and from the rejection of development and progress as grand narratives.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the academic-left, postcolonial reception of the theory; the core thinkers wrote little on aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning milieu and distrust of state power and security discourse; the core texts do not address it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is skeptical of representation and consensus procedures but has no view on how a head of state is chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Lyotard criticizes performativity and expert systems steering society by efficiency; a technocratic price-stability body fits that target. Inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the critique of essentialist national narratives, which undercuts claims to a fixed historic homeland.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning politics of adherents and Derrida's engagement with Marx; ownership is not treated as a natural right.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The movement broke with Marxist grand narratives and does not take a side on how to classify the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from postmodern scepticism of technocratic claims to certainty and of progress narratives.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the suspicion of state power and grand narratives of national security; not a topic the thinkers treated directly.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the postcolonial strand's critique of imperial domination and its defence of the dominated.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Foucault criticised the church's pastoral power but equally distrusted state power, so adherents are split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of unifying national symbols and consensus as covers for particular interests.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from its preference for local narratives and difference and its distrust of state violence.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from its valuing of local narratives, difference and dissensus over uniform systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Foucault's analysis treats sovereign, sacral power as a historical form of domination to be questioned, and divine legitimation is a grand narrative the movement doubts.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the movement's mainly academic-left politics, which favour redistribution over regressive-leaning tax design.

character-from-environment.rationale: Foucault in the 1971 debate with Chomsky doubted a fixed human nature and treated subjects as produced by discourse, institutions and power.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Foucault's work on power critiques sovereign power and its claims to stand outside norms; inferred from that rather than a stated rule.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of progress through technology as a grand narrative of modernity.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favour dissent and radical pluralism but do not take up constitutional design.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the critique of power, discourse and mass legitimating narratives, and the left-academic politics it was taken up in.

equal-parenting.rationale: Postmodern feminists were split between criticising gender norms in custody law and doubting rights presumptions; no stated position.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Postmodernism doubts Marxist grand narratives of history, so a class-struggle thesis is not endorsed in that form; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; postmodern thinkers were not committed to a position on agrarian reform.

refugee-return.rationale: Postcolonial and Foucauldian critiques of borders and displacement lean toward return rights; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Postmodernism treats national and ethnic identity as constructed and rejects claims built on it; inferred from its rejection of ethnic-nation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing deviance from orthodoxy is the kind of disciplinary power Foucault critiques; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Postmodern feminism opposes legal norms that discipline women's bodies; inferred from Foucault on power over bodies.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; postmodernism has no settled position on monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: It distrusts essentialist ideas of shared ancestry and unifying narratives; inferred from its rejection of civilizational union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: It favours local narratives and minority cultural self-expression; inferred from its support of minority language support.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Postmodern and postcolonial thought stresses difference and dissent within existing societies; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Postmodernism rejects single-cause grand narratives and stresses discourse and power over economic determinism; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; no settled postmodern position on competition law.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; no settled postmodern position on bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Its concern for minorities and dissent makes it wary of unconstrained majorities; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Postmodern feminism supports greater inclusion, though it questions fixed gender categories; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; no settled postmodern position.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; no settled postmodern position on trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; postmodernism is suspicious of both universal morals and planned motives, so it is split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: It distrusts vanguards and totalising emancipation narratives; inferred from its rejection of grand narratives.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: It criticises hierarchies sustained by institutions and power; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Postmodern thinkers reject grand narratives and Eurocentric history, and postcolonial uses favour plural, decentred accounts.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Postcolonial thought drawn from postmodernism rejects civilizing missions as discourses that legitimate domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from its view of nations as constructed by discourse and its suspicion of unifying national narratives.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from its multiculturalist and feminist uses, which favour remedies for underrepresented groups; no canonical text addresses admissions policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; Foucault and Derrida are critical of state power while Lyotard accepts capital's role, so adherents have no common line.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lyotard sees capitalism absorbing challenges while Derrida's Specters lists the new order's plagues; adherents are split on this.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from postcolonial critique of imperial legacies, which rejects special claims to influence over former colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; postcolonial uses favour autonomy for the formerly colonized but the philosophy offers no development programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Foucault resists unified class analysis and Derrida's New International stresses global solidarity; adherents lack a settled view. Inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from its feminist and multiculturalist politics, which treat discrimination as a form of power to be contested.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Foucault sees rights discourse as both a tool and a form of power, and Lyotard distrusts universal foundations; adherents are split. Inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Postcolonial thought, one of postmodernism's main political uses, questions colonial authority; inferred from that link, not from the core texts.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; inferred from their preference for dissent and plural participation over inherited authority.

minority-veto.rationale: Lyotard prizes dissensus and the rights of the minority voice, but no source endorses a veto over collective decisions, so this is split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Foucault holds that power invites resistance and endorses contesting abuse by institutions; the constitutional-trust framing is not theirs, so this is inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Postmodern thinkers distrust all centralized sovereignty, including legislatures, and did not address parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Late Derrida wrote on the animal question and criticized treatment of animals, but this is peripheral to the movement and mostly inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: No settled position; Derrida's animal writing criticized industrial animal use while the movement as a whole is silent.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from its suspicion of hierarchy and paternalist benevolence, which it reads as an exercise of power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Foucault held that power runs through all social relations, so withdrawal is not neutral, and his and Derrida's work is politically engaged.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Baudrillard and Lyotard describe media and commodified knowledge as reproducing the order; the claim is less central for other postmodernists.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Foucault's account of power operating through discourse and institutions, not only force, matches this; the class framing is Gramscian and inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Postcolonial strands accept something like it, but postmodernists distrust the Marxist grand narrative of structural exploitation, so they are split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from its stress on difference, multiculturalism and suspicion of fixed national identity.

party-own-road.rationale: Postmodernists broke with party-based communism and reject its metanarrative, so the question has little purchase.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; the movement offers no development theory.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from its skepticism of national narratives and sovereignty claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Postcolonial strands may sympathize, but the movement does not endorse group leadership by descent and is split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Postmodern thinkers were largely anti-authoritarian and left-leaning; the constitutional framing is inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Lyotard and Foucault criticized both Soviet communism and Western institutions, but the equivalence thesis is not theirs and the academic left is split on it.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the academic-left milieu, which treats slavery as the central cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Postmodernists question official memory and monuments, yet favour keeping contested memory visible; adherents are split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; postmodern feminism stresses the construction of gender, which does not settle this.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from postmodern feminism's focus on gendered power relations, which resists a symmetry framing.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Its skepticism of universal narratives and Enlightenment universalism fits cultural pluralism in forms of government.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from its suspicion of institutional power and discipline, which Foucault analysed in the military and prison.

paid-care-work.rationale: Postmodern feminism is sympathetic to revaluing gendered labour; not a stated position of the core thinkers.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's suspicion of inherited norms and hierarchies as products of power; it does not address filial duty directly.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from Lyotard's critique of performativity and expert legitimation of knowledge, which treats credentialing as an exercise of power.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The core thinkers do not address this economic question and the movement is not united on it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from Foucault's critique of institutional regulation of sexuality and family norms; not addressed directly.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Postmodern theory favors dissent and plural local voices but offers no settled view on how representation should work.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's mostly academic-left and anti-neoliberal reception, including Derrida's critique of the post-1989 market order.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; neutral is inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; neutral is inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from its valuing of difference and local narratives over a single standard, as in postcolonial and multicultural uses.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; its distrust of nationalism and of capital pull in different directions.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its treatment of institutions as embodying power relations, as taken up in postcolonial and critical race scholarship; not stated by the core thinkers.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Baudrillard's and Lyotard's critiques of the commodification of signs and knowledge; the audit's core thinkers do not state a welfare judgment.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from Derrida's condemnation of the violence and inequality of the new world order and the movement's distrust of great-power claims.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from its suspicion of grand narratives used to justify domination, and its break with Soviet Communism; not addressed directly.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lyotard argues that capital and performativity increasingly govern knowledge and legitimacy, and Foucault ties power to institutions; inferred to corporate power.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from suspicion of state sovereignty and of national narratives.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Foucault's biopolitics treats state management of population and reproduction critically; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from distrust of exclusionary identities and boundaries, though it favors local narratives.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the academic-left reception and concern with inequality.

democratic-peace.rationale: It doubts universal narratives of progress, including that one regime type brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Foucault and Derrida treat law as an expression of power and distinguish it from justice, so legality alone confers no duty; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Postcolonial uses are wary of intervention, though Foucault himself backed some humanitarian action, so the 'any reason' wording is tentative.

industrial-unions.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Its critique of grand narratives and essentialist identity rejects conspiratorial accounts of minorities; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Foucault's history of sexuality and queer theory question state regulation of intimate life.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Lyotard's report argues the public should have free access to memory and data banks.

local-production.rationale: Its preference for local narratives and small-scale difference suggests localism; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Foucault's micro-resistance and the preference for local, plural struggles favor small informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: It is suspicious of sovereignty and of fixed national authority; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: It rejects essentialist, unified identity categories, so shared religion defining a nation is opposed; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: postmodern thought distrusts hierarchies and universal orders, so ritual submission to a leading power runs against it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: its concern with inequality and difference favors redistribution, but the thinkers did not address regional revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed; Derrida's Marx-inflected critique of capital points one way, while the suspicion of any totalizing economic program points the other.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: Derrida's Specters of Marx attacks post-1989 triumphalism about liberal capitalism, and the milieu is left-leaning, though not pro-Soviet.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; Lyotard criticises performativity and market logic in institutions, but there is no stated view on who should deliver public services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: it rejects grand narratives such as secularization and progress, so it would not accept that religion simply fades with better conditions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the narrative of progress through modernity and its critique of capitalism's performativity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the postmodern feminism the movement fed, which links gendered subordination to institutions and power structures.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: academic-left postmodern feminism and its critique of the family as a site of power point to support, though the core thinkers did not propose it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from its support for minority languages and distrust of national homogeneity, which makes official purging unattractive.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from postcolonial and multiculturalist applications, which stress recognition and the rights of minorities against dominant states.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: it favors local narratives and small-scale difference, but the thinkers did not endorse property-holding communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: it opposes assimilationist, homogenizing national projects, so state-steered majority settlement conflicts with it.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: Lyotard rejects all grand narratives, Marxist ones included, but the milieu accepted neither liberal capitalist triumphalism nor Soviet communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the movement's suspicion of grand narratives and essentialist origin myths used to ground claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Postmodern thinkers study how discourse shapes truth but did not defend denial; inferred rejection, since Lyotard and Foucault wrote as victims-of-power critics.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Foucault's history of sexuality treats such norms as products of disciplinary power, and queer theory grew from this work.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Postmodern thought favours dissent and local narratives over enforced consensus, and Foucault was an activist against state repression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from its critique of institutional power over knowledge and its defence of dissent.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Postcolonial thought, a main political use of these ideas, rejects colonial exploitation; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; neutral is inferred from that.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from its scepticism of religious metanarratives as grounds of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the preference for local narratives, dissent and bottom-up contestation of power, though the texts do not endorse a participatory programme.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Postmodern feminism and multiculturalism treat identity and oppression as produced by overlapping discourses; inferred from that reception.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Queer theory and postmodern feminism, drawing on Foucault, treat gender as constructed; the legal question itself is inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Foucault's biopower analysis cuts both ways on control over death, and adherents are split; neutral inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It broke with Marxist grand narratives but its academic adherents remained largely on the left; adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Lyotard and others reject the Marxist grand narrative that frames alienation, while Derrida keeps parts of Marx; adherents are split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from its multiculturalist and postcolonial reception, which resists essentialising cultures.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of all grand narratives, religious ones included, as grounds of legitimacy.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; multiculturalists and critics of institutional neutrality are split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its concern with institutional power silencing the less powerful.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed by the core thinkers; neutral inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the concern with inequality and the critique of progress narratives that justify unevenness.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; neutral is inferred from that.

missingStatements.text: Claims to objective knowledge are shaped by the interests of those in power.
missingStatements.rationale: The inseparability of knowledge and power is a founding claim of Lyotard and Foucault and the core of the postmodern critique.

missingStatements.text: There are universal truths about morality and society that hold across all cultures.
missingStatements.rationale: Postmodernism is defined by its rejection of universal, foundational truths and grand narratives in favor of local, plural ones.

notes: Postmodern thinkers rarely stated policy positions, so most economic and many social answers are inferred from the left politics of the movement's academic adherents and marked low. Foucault's views shifted (more Marxist in 1971, closer to ethics and interest in liberalism late in life), and Rorty's 'postmodernist bourgeois liberalism' would answer several governance questions more favorably to liberal democracy and markets. Critics such as Habermas and Chomsky charge the tradition with relativism; adherents dispute that label.
